name: EWF World Championship
epitaph: EWF's own top title from its founding show onward: 16 structured reign changes from Kraven's win of the founding battle royal (2001) to a three-way rights transfer settled at the fed's fourth PPV (2005) and Kraven's third reign (2007).

name: EWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: EWF's own tag championship: 29 structured reign changes from its first holders (2001) through a commissioner-awarded reign at the fed's third PPV (2005).

name: EWF Fuck the World Championship
epitaph: A hardcore-styled title carrying a profane name the fed used without euphemism on its own site: 28 structured reign changes from a self-awarded first reign (2001) to a vacancy declared at the reactivation show (2007).

name: EWF Evolution Championship
epitaph: Billed by the fed itself as the spiritual successor to a defunct "Konstantynopol" title: 22 structured reign changes from a tournament final (2002) to Oscar Knifer's reign (2007).

name: EWF Daemusin Championship
epitaph: A title renamed and revived in EWF in 2009 as the self-described "spiritual continuator" of a 1999-2001 predecessor-federation belt (PCW Stolica); only its one attested EWF-era holder is structured here, from his own roster bio.

name: EWF/PCW Polish Championship
epitaph: One of the fed's longest-running belts by its own record, tracing back to a 1999 predecessor federation (PCW); this collection structures only its EWF-era reign chain (16 changes, 2002-2004), holding the earlier PCW-era ledger as prose on the title's own served page.

name: EWF Puchar Szczęściarza
epitaph: A periodic "Lucky Guy's Cup" battle-royal/tournament trophy, awarded five times across 2004-2009 by the fed's own record; its second edition's scheduled match was cancelled outright and no winner was named.
notes: Its second edition, scheduled for PPV "Kwietniowa Anarchia III" (17 April 2005), was cancelled outright and named no winner.
